tool_input.description: Empirically verify ArithmeticException and lenient/strict parse behavior

result:
`DateUtilsAgentTest` is the only `*AgentTest.java` in the project right now, and all 103 tests pass.

Created `src/test/java/org/apache/commons/lang3/time/DateUtilsAgentTest.java` (JUnit 5 Jupiter, no lambdas/diamond operator/underscored literals, self-contained). It covers all public methods of `DateUtils`: the `add*`, `ceiling`, `getFragmentIn*`, `isSame*`, `iterator`, `parseDate`/`parseDateStrictly`, `round`, `set*`, `toCalendar`, `toLocalDateTime`/`toOffsetDateTime`/`toZonedDateTime`, `truncate`, `truncatedCompareTo`/`truncatedEquals`, and the constants/public constructor — including boundary cases (DST-safe UTC/default-zone fixtures, iterator exhaustion/`remove()`, invalid range styles, oversized years triggering `ArithmeticException`, lenient-vs-strict parsing, out-of-range `set*` values) and error cases (`NullPointerException`, `ClassCastException`, `IllegalArgumentException`, `ParseException`).

Two initial assumptions (drawn from stale/misleading javadoc examples) didn't match actual behavior and were corrected after empirical verification against the compiled library: `GregorianCalendar.add(YEAR, …)` pins Feb 29 to Feb 28 rather than rolling to March 1, and `getFragmentInMinutes` with a `MONTH` fragment includes whole days converted to minutes (not just the hour/minute-of-day component as one javadoc example states).
